text: Grey Market wagons past the Sunken Steeple — salt and nails, fair but sharp.
Lantern crows stole the wicks again. The wayfinder pays buttons for white tail feathers.
The masons seek 200 wood — the east wall remembers.
Moth-deer sign in the high clearings. Good luck for a year, says the butcher.
Dren Salt's carters mending the west bridge. Toll is up a nail a wheel.
Moon-moths thick on the Grove — a good picking night, say the foragers.
A poacher tapped the watchfire twice last night. Bread, not chain, says the mooncleric.
Old Bell's bent clapper still on the market stall. Touch it for luck — one button.
Bristle boars rooting the south kiln-pads. The mason complains. The butcher smiles.
Grey light coming. The builders say grey days set mortar best.
Joren's hat still hangs by the hall door. Nobody touches it. Everybody checks.
Two knocks answered by two knocks in the treeline. Grandmothers hurry the children home.
The Lantern Towns pay premium for blue-veined timber. Everybody sells. Nobody forgot.
Pond gone dark three nights running? Rest it. Overdrawn land goes pale.
